name: Metal Backend
description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Normal composite (MB-4, enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device only) runs the composite_normal kernel in place on the backdrop's tiles, piece by piece from CompositeMap, with CoreRaster's sourceOver rule, opacity check and clip (an evicted backdrop tile is brought back to a texture first and the budget enforced after; a source that is the backdrop is read from a snapshot). The eleven other separable modes (MB-5) run as variants of the same in-place path, one blendSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's blend formula, with .blendSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-6). Hue, saturation, color and luminosity (MB-9) run through the same in-place path as one blendNonSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's Lum, Sat, SetLum, SetSat and ClipColor, but .blendNonSeparable is not enabled at init (MB-10) and the public composite throws unsupported for those modes; a package parity hook enables the family on a read-write tier 2 device. The opaque-row fast path (MB-6): under .normal at opacity exactly 1, the rows of a piece whose stored Float16 source alphas are all exactly 1 (read from the source tile, resident or staged) are copied onto the backdrop tile with blits instead of the kernel, split by OpaqueRows, with pixels equal to the CPU backend's copy. Resample (MB-8) runs bilinear and lanczos3 on the GPU as two separable passes of ResampleTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's pass order (the source read like `read`, resident tiles merged with shadows, and uploaded from the CPU), scattered into a new surface with components clamped to the finite half range; an invalid size throws the CPU backend's error, and a valid size whose largest buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength throws unsupported(.resample) with the backend still healthy, so the caller resamples on the CPU backend. Adjust (MB-13, MB-14; .adjust enabled at init) runs every tone adjustment (exposure, levels, curves, white balance, contrast, highlights/shadows) through the adjust_tone kernel tile by tile into a new surface, reading AdjustTable's per-channel gains, per-channel table with its two octave tables or luminance gain table on unpremultiplied values with CoreRaster's alpha guard (an evicted source tile through a temporary texture) and the CPU backend's errors for invalid parameters. Gaussian blur (MB-11) runs as two separable blur_pass passes of BlurTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's order (across, then down) with clamp-to-edge taps, scattered into a new surface by the resample scatter kernel; sigma 0 returns the pixels unchanged and an invalid sigma throws the CPU backend's error. Unsharp mask (MB-12) runs in one command buffer as blur_pass across the rows and then blur_unsharp, which finishes the blur down the columns and sharpens each premultiplied component in Float32 with UnsharpRule's parameters (the rule UnsharpRule.apply mirrors), scattered into a new surface; invalid parameters and an overflowing result throw the CPU backend's errors; .blur is enabled at init, and blur and unsharp throw unsupported while the backend is unhealthy and, with the backend still healthy, for a valid image whose whole-image buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength, so the caller runs them on the CPU backend. Clone through a mask (MB-15; .retouch enabled at init) packs the source, read like `read`, and the mask's coverage into whole-image buffers and runs retouch_clone into each tile of a new surface with CoreRaster's clone rule, the CPU backend's errors in its order, and offsets whose sources are all off the image returning the pixels unchanged; an image over maxBufferLength throws unsupported, and so does clone while the backend is unhealthy. Non-separable blends stay off at init until MB-10.
